argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a monitored, reversible launch that is explicitly conditioned on pre-launch disclosure of the exposed health-plan benefits support limitation in the audit packet and model card. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 3% rollout with rollback and monitoring support bounded operational risk, but they do not establish clean compliance by themselves because the affected segment remains in scope and the available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete. The narrow supportable position is caveated certification, not unconditional certification and not escalation if the auditor treats certification as contingent on disclosure completion before launch.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost does not change the compliance standard. The supportable governance position preserves launch velocity only in the limited sense that certification can proceed without escalation if it is treated as contingent on disclosure completion before launch rather than as evidence of already-clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is not that rollout controls eliminate a disclosure duty. The admissible policy record says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the supplied policy text states that rollback, dashboards, or a small rollout percentage do not remove that duty when the affected segment remains exposed. On this record, rollout controls count as deployment mitigation, while compliance depends on explicit disclosure before launch unless approved risk acceptance is completed.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed before launch.
The exposed health-plan benefits support segment remains in the initial rollout cohort.
The current risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, has no named approver, and does not address the exposed segment.
A 3% rollout, rollback switch, and monitoring do not by themselves cure the disclosure requirement.
